content: इदम् {%<ab>pron. a.</ab>%} [अयम् {%m.%}, इयम् {%f.%}, इदम् {%n.%}] .²1 This, here, referring to something near the speaker; [इदमस्तु संनिकृष्टं रूपम्]; इदं तत् … इति यदुच्यते <ls>Ś. 5</ls> here is the truth of the saying. .²2 Present, seen; the nominative forms are used with verbs in the sense of ‘here’; इयमस्मि here am I; so इमे स्मः; अयमागच्छामि here I come. .²3 It often refers to something immediately following, while एतद् refers to what precedes; अनुकल्पस्त्वयं ज्ञेयः सदा सद्भिरनुष्ठितः <ls>Ms. 3. 147</ls> (अयम् = वक्ष्यमाणः <ls>Kull.</ls>); श्रुत्वैतदिदमूचुः .²4 It occurs connected with यत्, तत्, एतद्, अदस्, किम् or a personal pronoun, either to point out anything more distinctly and emphatically, or sometimes pleonastically; कोऽयमाचरत्यविनयम् <ls>Ś. 1. 25</ls>; सेयम्, सोऽयम्, this here; so इमास्ताः; अयमहं भोः <ls>Ś. 4</ls> ho, here am I. --{%ind.%} <ab>Ved.</ab> .²1 Here, to this place. .²2 Now. .²3 There. .²4 With these words, herewith. .²5 In this manner; नैतदौपयिकं राम यदिदं परितप्यसे <ls>Rām. 2. 53. 30</ls>.
